clue.text: Still, one begins to miss the phone

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word miss is wanted, the start of that word

parts.note: a mobile is a cellular telephone

explanation.surface: Someone stops still as the first ring of the phone goes unanswered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is motionless, unable or not moving.

clue.text: Understand nothing goes with fashionable colour

parts.note: in means trendy
dig is slang for understand, as in 'do you dig?'
O resembles zero

explanation.surface: Grasping that a trendy colour has nothing behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet shade of the spectrum.

clue.text: Curse a noisy queue on the motorway

indicators.note: noisy means what follows is said out loud

parts.note: a line on the M, the British motorway prefix, said as M-a-line

explanation.surface: A loud traffic jam on the motorway is cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are named M1, M25 and so on; a queue (line) on one is 'M a line'.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign is to slander or speak ill of someone, close to cursing.

clue.text: A mousse on black bread!

indicators.note: on means the A-plus-mousse part is placed after the black abbreviation

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a styling mousse is a hair gel

explanation.surface: Chocolate mousse spread on a dark loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll.

clue.text: Weapon made from pine on front of ship

parts.note: to pine is to long for
the bow is the forward part of a ship

explanation.surface: An arm built from pine wood on the prow of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A longbow is a tall English bow used in medieval warfare.

clue.text: Increase the pace at university

parts.note: a pace is a single step
in British usage a student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: A call to quicken the pace while studying at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British convention, especially for Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up output is to raise or boost it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: High flying river guide?

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England
a pilot guides ships into harbour

explanation.surface: A river guide who also flies high.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a famous trout river in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft at the edge of their performance, often at altitude.

clue.text: Exercises for journalists include drink!

indicators.note: the word for reporters wraps around the word for a sip

parts.note: the press collectively
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Reporters' workout comes with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups are push-ups, a floor workout routine.

clue.text: Messed around with empty title in design of red top

indicators.note: the emptied word is placed within the rearranged letters
the letters of red top are redesigned
empty means the inside of the word title is removed

explanation.surface: A tabloid with no headline gets a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' rearranges RED TOP to POTRED; 'empty' leaves TE of title, which goes 'in'. A red top is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to idle about doing small tasks, aimless activity.

clue.text: Very careful if student is in editing letters

indicators.note: the student's letter sits within the other rearranged letters
the letters of editing are taken as material to be rearranged

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A scrupulous student tidies up correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' tells you to rearrange the word editing, giving DIIGENT; 'is in' puts L (learner) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent worker is painstaking and conscientious, a synonym for very careful.

clue.text: A second broadcast gets the go ahead

parts.note: sent out, as a signal is transmitted

explanation.surface: A programme aired for a second time gets official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or permission, the same as giving the go-ahead.

clue.text: This is what you get when the wheels come off!

definitions.text: This is what you get when the wheels come off!

parts.words: This is what you get when the wheels come off!
parts.note: a disaster idiom read literally: with the wheels removed the rod they turn on is left

explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the shaft on which wheels rotate, left bare once they are removed.

clue.text: A viewer needs one in glasses case

parts.note: a single eyepiece of a pair of protective goggles
a box is a container or case

explanation.surface: A spectator requires a spectacle case for their lenses.
explanation.walkthrough: GOGGLEBOX is British slang for a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: A television is something watched, and slang treats the set itself as a viewer.

clue.text: Almost went out of fashion!

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its end

parts.note: passed, as time goes by or a person goes past

explanation.surface: Someone nearly left as the style became dated.
explanation.walkthrough: PASSED is missing its last letter, so PASSE remains, a borrowed French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé describes something no longer stylish, outmoded.

clue.text: Loud and deep is the current

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
low, as a deep voice is low-pitched

explanation.surface: A noisy, deep river current.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a stream or movement of water, its flow.

clue.text: The sort of person to put a listening device under the bed?

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the device below the bedding word

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
a bug is a hidden microphone

explanation.surface: A spy who hides a microphone beneath the mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: LITTERBUG is US/informal for a person who drops rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is someone who carelessly drops rubbish in public.

clue.text: Sun screen?

parts.note: not a lotion but something that blocks out the sun, as the moon does when passing in front of it

explanation.definitionFit: During a solar eclipse the moon blocks the sunlight, screening the sun.

clue.text: In favour of Latin, provided one could start being productive

parts.note: pro means for
if means provided that
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word could is used

explanation.surface: Supporting Latin, if one could begin to be fruitful.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolific means highly fruitful, producing much work.

clue.text: Able to read a letter, I get worried!

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fretting that they can read a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person can read and write.

clue.text: Make merry with one in the duty list

indicators.note: the numeral is set within the word for the schedule

parts.note: a roster lists who is on duty when
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Have fun with someone on the work rota.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, to have a boisterous good time.

clue.text: Regretted promoting the last one, as ill-mannered

indicators.note: promoting means moving the final letter up one place

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Being sorry about promoting the newest recruit seemed impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: In RUED the last letter E moves up past D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude means impolite.

clue.text: Many plans are executed

indicators.note: executed in the sense of beheaded, so the word loses its head

parts.note: plots are schemes or plans

explanation.surface: Lots of schemes are carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like 'carried out' but means beheaded: PLOTS loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots means a great number of, a colloquial synonym for many.

clue.text: Rent day precedes personal disappointment

parts.note: to let is to rent out
own means belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Paying rent day brings personal disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is a disappointing anticlimax.

clue.text: In which Hamlet's beaten and leaves undisturbed

indicators.note: in which signals the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A version of the play in which Hamlet loses and walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: To let be means to leave alone without interfering.

clue.text: The way a sibling sees inactivity

parts.note: st is street, a way
sis is a sister

explanation.surface: How a sister views idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stagnation or no change.

clue.text: Belgian city, say, caught in deception

indicators.note: the abbreviation is trapped within the word for a falsehood

parts.note: a lie is a deception
e.g. means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: A city in Belgium found out in a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a major city in the French-speaking part of Belgium.

clue.text: Damage caused in time by sorely tried people

indicators.note: sorely suggests the word tried is badly hurt, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: men as people in general

explanation.surface: Harm done over time by people who have been badly tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorely' is the anagram signal: the surface reads tried people as hard-pressed folk, but the word tried is just raw letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss, a synonym for damage.

clue.text: Daft? That's taking in granny!

indicators.note: taking in means holding the grandmother inside

parts.note: i.e. stands for that is
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Is it silly to deceive a grandmother?
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' looks like deceiving granny but means containing NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless.

clue.text: Way of cooking meat in iron container?

indicators.note: the meat goes inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Fe, the chemical symbol for iron, acts as the container
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Roasting a joint in a cast-iron pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé cooking means dousing food in spirit and setting it alight, a culinary method.

clue.text: After a short time, misses treacle!

indicators.note: after puts the girls' word behind the short time

parts.note: mo, short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'
lasses are young women, or misses

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, some girls take the syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is dark syrup from sugar refining, the American term for treacle.

clue.text: Cloth covers in classical exterior grey

indicators.note: the covers of each word are its first and last letters, picked from the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Fabric with a classical grey finish on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' is a common term for the priesthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is a metonym for ordained priests and ministers, after their clerical dress.

clue.text: Steering wheels given numbers

indicators.note: wheels as a verb, to turn round, so the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Steering wheels are labelled with figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers are whole numbers.
